title: Introduce delta scorer and release-note contextualizer
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds an automated delta-scoring pipeline that ranks model profile changes by user-impact signals
Introduces a contextualizer that synthesizes concise release-note bullets and example prompts/outputs for each high-priority delta
Backfills scores for recent 90-day model releases and exposes an API for release-note candidates
description: Context: manual changelog curation is a recurring bottleneck during model rollouts and makes it hard for engineers and product to prioritize follow-up work. Motivation: automate prioritization of model metadata changes (perf regressions/improvements, tokenizer changes, API surface changes) so that release notes surface actionable items and reduce reviewer overhead. What this PR does: 1) Adds a delta-scoring service that consumes profile diffs and computes a single 'delta_score' per change using weighted signals (perf magnitude, sample-level regression count, dataset overlap, stability signature, API-compat flags, and recent customer impact markers). 2) Introduces a release-note contextualizer that converts a high-score delta into 1-3 concise bullets plus an example prompt and expected model output snippet to help SREs/docs. 3) Wires the outputs into the existing changelog-assembler: candidates are emitted to the /release-candidates API and the console shows a ranked list for editors. Design notes: scoring is a hybrid rule + small-model scorer (lightweight instruct model running in cheap CPU tier) — weights are configurable via the registry config and backed by a Linear ticket for tuning. The contextualizer uses a compact prompt template and extracts deterministic snippets; fallbacks use a template renderer when the small-model confidence is low. Data migration and rollout: adds a nullable delta_score column to model_profile_deltas and a release_candidates table. Migration is backward-compatible; system will not change UI behavior until feature flag 'release_context_v1' is flipped. Backfill: script backfills 90 days of profile diffs and emits candidates; backfill ran in staging and its results were spot-checked. Tests: unit tests for scoring heuristics, integration tester for release-candidates endpoint, and end-to-end smoke that renders candidate bullets. Security & privacy: contextualizer runs only on metadata and synthetic examples; no customer PII is sent to external services. Related work: ENG-2109 (signal framework), PR #33109 (micro-changelog plumbing) and ENG-1965 (profile-stability signatures). Checklist: [x] scoring core implemented [x] contextualizer model + template [x] API and db migration [x] backfill script + dry-run mode [x] docs updated in registry readme [x] e2e tests and CI green Migration steps for operators: run the migration, toggle feature flag in console, run backfill with --dry-run to validate. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to weight defaults and the small-model confidence threshold; we intentionally keep weights conservative for initial rollout.

notes_for_ops: Migration adds nullable column; migration is safe to run online. Backfill should be started with --concurrency=4 and monitored; default weight config lives in config/delta_weights.yaml. If noisy candidates appear, reduce perf weight and increase stability penalty. To disable: flip feature flag 'release_context_v1' in the console.
examples: Sample candidate output: [Improved tokenization for token X leading to +3% BLEU on dataset A] -> bullets: 'Tokenization change reduced off-by-one splits for X, improving structured output on dataset A (approx +3% BLEU). Suggest smoke test: run evaluation suite on dataset A and verify no new regressions.' Example prompt: 'Summarize differences in handling token X and provide an example input+output before/after.'
Fallback rendering: plain template usage when model confidence < 0.6: 'Change detected: <short description>. Recommended action: run evaluation on affected datasets.'
